assumedContext: Shares outstanding (~340m) is DERIVED: buybacks of roughly USD 6.5bn since late 2021 have reduced the count by about 30% from roughly 485m.

Net debt (~USD 18.5bn) is DERIVED and is the weakest input in this dossier. It implies roughly 2.6x FY2026E adjusted EBITDA, consistent with a reported debt-to-equity ratio of 3.63 and with the Energy Harbor acquisition and the buyback programme both being debt-assisted.

findings.claim: Capital return has been aggressive and effective: roughly USD 6.5bn of share repurchases since late 2021, reducing the share count by about 30%, with a remaining USD 1.2bn authorisation expected to be exhausted by the end of 2027.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Retiring 30% of the share count is the single most shareholder-friendly action taken by any company in this batch, and it stands in direct contrast to PPC, which increased its share count by 62% in the same period.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-reference to the PPC dossier

findings.claim: But it was funded partly with debt, and the leverage is the risk. Estimated net debt of roughly USD 18.5bn against FY2026E adjusted EBITDA of USD 7.2bn is about 2.6x — manageable in isolation, and materially less so against merchant earnings exposed to a softening ERCOT curve with 28% of the 2028 book open.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: This is the combination that produced the 30% de-rating and it is worth stating plainly: a levered balance sheet against cyclical merchant cash flows means the equity is a geared claim on the ERCOT forward curve. A 10% fall in merchant margin moves equity value by considerably more than 10%.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: At USD 139.80 and roughly 340m shares the market capitalisation is about USD 47.5bn. Adding estimated net debt gives an enterprise value of roughly USD 66bn, or about 9.2x FY2026E adjusted EBITDA of USD 7.2bn.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: A price-earnings multiple is excluded from this dossier deliberately. Q2 GAAP net income of USD 305m against adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.767bn shows how far hedge marks distort reported earnings; any P/E computed from them would be noise presented as precision.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Justified price-to-book is also excluded. After roughly USD 6.5bn of buybacks and a debt-to-equity ratio of 3.63, book equity is small relative to enterprise value and carries little information about intrinsic worth. The valuation in Phase 5 uses discounted cash flow, EV/EBITDA and a sum-of-the-parts.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: On enterprise multiples Vistra sits mid-pack in this batch at about 9.2x, alongside PPC at roughly 9.2x, above Metlen at 7.7x, and far below Siemens Energy at 17x and GE Vernova at about 40x. On cash yield it is the cheapest here by a wide margin.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-references to the other dossiers in this batch

risks.text: Estimated net debt of roughly USD 18.5bn against cyclical merchant earnings makes the equity a geared claim on the ERCOT forward curve; a 10% fall in merchant margin moves equity value by considerably more.
Net debt and the share count are both derived rather than sourced, and net debt is 39% of market capitalisation.

conclusions: Capital return has been the most shareholder-friendly in this batch: roughly USD 6.5bn of buybacks since late 2021, retiring about 30% of the share count, against PPC increasing its count by 62% over a comparable period.

But it was partly debt-funded. Estimated net debt of roughly USD 18.5bn against USD 7.2bn of FY2026E adjusted EBITDA is about 2.6x — manageable in isolation and much less so against merchant earnings with 28% of the 2028 book open.
That combination is what produced the 30% de-rating. A levered balance sheet against cyclical cash flows means the equity is a geared claim on the ERCOT forward curve.
At roughly 9.2x FY2026E EBITDA the enterprise multiple is mid-pack in this batch, but the roughly 9.1% free-cash-flow-before-growth yield is the cheapest here by a wide margin.

Both a price-earnings multiple and a justified price-to-book are excluded deliberately: hedge marks make GAAP earnings uninformative, and after USD 6.5bn of buybacks book equity carries little information about intrinsic worth.
thesisImpact: Phase 4 establishes that the equity is a geared claim on merchant power prices with an excellent contracted core and an exceptional cash yield. Phase 5 values it on discounted cash flow, enterprise multiple and a sum-of-the-parts that separates the contracted nuclear from the merchant gas and the coal.
